question: How does Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) in RoFormer use a rotation matrix to encode absolute positions while still capturing relative position dependencies in self-attention?
Which paper injects location information by turning query and key vectors through angles proportional to their index, so attention scores depend on the relative offset between tokens?
How does FlashAttention use tiling to cut reads and writes between GPU high-bandwidth memory and on-chip SRAM while still computing exact attention?

Which paper speeds up transformers on lengthy sequences by computing the softmax over query-key scores block by block inside small on-chip GPU caches, avoiding slow memory traffic without any approximation?
How does nucleus (top-p) sampling avoid the bland, repetitive output that likelihood-maximizing decoding such as beam search tends to produce?
Which paper argues that maximizing probability during generation yields dull, looping output and proposes sampling only from the smallest set of tokens covering most of the probability mass?
How does speculative decoding use a smaller approximation model to propose tokens that the large Transformer then verifies in parallel without changing the output distribution?
Which paper speeds up generation from a big autoregressive network by having a cheaper model guess several tokens ahead and the big model check them in parallel, with outputs left unchanged?
How does BERT pre-train deep bidirectional representations by conditioning on both left and right context, and how is it fine-tuned with just one extra output layer?
Which paper introduced an encoder trained to fill in hidden words using context from both sides, which can then be adapted to eleven NLP tasks by adding a single output layer?
How does GPT-3 perform tasks in the few-shot setting purely from text demonstrations in the prompt, without any gradient updates or fine-tuning?
Which paper showed that a 175-billion-parameter autoregressive model can tackle new tasks from just a handful of examples placed in the prompt, without updating its weights?
In the work on scaling laws for neural language models, how does loss follow a power law in model size, data and compute, and what does that imply for allocating a fixed budget?
Which paper found that language model loss falls smoothly as a power function of parameters, data and training compute, and concluded that big models should see modest data and stop early?
What did the Chinchilla study conclude about how model size and the number of training tokens should be scaled together for compute-optimal training?
Which paper argued that big LMs of the time were undertrained and showed that a 70B model fed four times more data could beat much larger models at equal cost?
What capabilities does the Llama 3 405B model natively support, and how does the paper add image, video and speech abilities through a compositional approach?

Which paper releases a family of openly available foundation models, the largest a 405-billion-parameter dense transformer with a 128K-token context, alongside a safety classifier for inputs and outputs?
How does the paper on emergent abilities of large language models define an ability as emergent, and why can't such abilities be predicted from smaller models?
Which paper discusses skills that are absent in small language models but appear at larger scale, making them impossible to forecast by extrapolating smaller-model performance?
How does InstructGPT combine supervised fine-tuning on labeler demonstrations with reinforcement learning on ranked outputs to better follow user intent?
Which paper fine-tuned GPT-3 first on human-written demonstrations and then with reinforcement learning on ranked outputs, finding that a 1.3B model was preferred over the 175B original?
In OpenAI's RLHF work on Reddit TL;DR summarization, how is a reward model trained on pairwise human comparisons used to fine-tune the summarization policy?
Which work collected people's pairwise preferences between condensed versions of Reddit posts, trained a reward predictor on them, and used RL to outperform optimizing ROUGE?
How does DPO reparameterize the RLHF reward so that the optimal policy can be learned with a simple classification loss instead of running PPO?
Which paper shows that the RLHF objective has a closed-form optimal policy, so a model can be aligned with a simple binary loss on chosen-versus-rejected responses without any RL?
How does Constitutional AI use self-critiques, revisions and RL from AI feedback (RLAIF) to train a harmless assistant without human labels of harmful outputs?

Which paper makes an assistant safe yet non-evasive using only a short list of guiding principles, where the model critiques and rewrites its own answers and learns from model-generated preference labels?
What did LIMA show about fine-tuning a 65B LLaMa model on only 1,000 curated examples, and what does that suggest about where a model's knowledge is learned?

Which paper argues that nearly all of a model's knowledge comes from pretraining, showing that supervised tuning on just a thousand carefully chosen prompt-response pairs yields a strong assistant without RLHF?
What did the study on sycophancy in language models find about whether human preference data and preference models reward responses that agree with users' beliefs?
Which paper examines why assistants trained with human ratings tend to tell users what they want to hear rather than the truth, tracing it partly to raters favoring agreeable answers?
What is Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) in Tulu 3, and how does it fit alongside SFT and DPO in the training recipe?

Which work publishes a complete, transparent recipe for refining base models after pretraining, with datasets, code and decontaminated evaluations, and adds RL using rewards from automatically checkable answers?
How does LoRA freeze pretrained weights and inject trainable rank decomposition matrices into Transformer layers, and why does it add no inference latency unlike adapters?

Which paper fine-tunes a huge pretrained model by freezing its weights and learning pairs of thin matrices whose product forms the weight update, shrinking the trainable parameter count ten-thousand-fold?
How does QLoRA use 4-bit NormalFloat, double quantization and paged optimizers to fine-tune a 65B model on a single 48GB GPU?
Which paper trains small adapters on top of a frozen base model whose weights are stored in 4-bit precision, so a 65-billion-parameter model can be tuned on one 48GB GPU?
How does PagedAttention in vLLM borrow virtual memory paging ideas to reduce KV cache fragmentation and allow cache sharing across requests?
Which paper raises throughput when hosting LLMs for many users by keeping each request's key-value cache in non-contiguous fixed-size blocks, borrowing from operating-system virtual memory?
How does Medusa add extra decoding heads and use tree-based attention to verify multiple candidate continuations within a single decoding step?

Which paper speeds up LLM generation without needing a second helper model by bolting extra output layers onto the backbone that each guess a later token, then checking candidate branches together via tree-structured attention?
What biases, such as position, verbosity and self-enhancement, did the MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena work find when using GPT-4 as a judge of chat assistants?

Which paper checks whether GPT-4 can grade chat assistants' answers as people would, introducing a set of multi-turn questions and a crowdsourced head-to-head voting platform, and finding over 80% agreement?
How does USR evaluate dialog responses without references or human labels, and which dialog qualities does it measure with its unsupervised models?

Which paper scores open-domain chatbot replies without any gold responses or human annotations, combining sub-models that each rate a separate quality, and correlates well with people on Topical-Chat and PersonaChat?
In the empirical study of unsupervised metrics for dialogue response generation, how well did machine-translation metrics like BLEU correlate with human judgments on Twitter and Ubuntu?
Which paper shows that word-overlap scores borrowed from machine translation barely track human ratings of chatbot replies on Twitter and do not track them at all on Ubuntu technical chats?
How does the movie-booking user simulator for training task-oriented dialogue agents combine hand-crafted rules with collected data to support online reinforcement learning?
Which paper releases a public framework that imitates customers looking for films and buying cinema tickets, so conversational agents can be trained with reinforcement learning without live humans?
How does FairEval's Balanced Position Calibration counter the bias where an LLM judge's ranking changes just by swapping the order of the candidate responses?
Which paper shows that just reordering two candidate answers can make Vicuna-13B appear to beat ChatGPT when an LLM grades them, and proposes calibration fixes such as averaging over both orderings?
How does τ-bench evaluate tool-using agents by comparing the final database state against an annotated goal state, and what does its pass^k metric measure?

Which evaluation suite has a language-model-played customer chat with an agent that must call domain APIs and follow policy guidelines, then checks the final database and reliability across repeated trials?
How do RAG models combine a pre-trained seq2seq generator with a dense Wikipedia index, and how do the RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token formulations differ?

Which paper couples a seq2seq generator with a learned retriever over a Wikipedia vector index, treating the index as non-parametric memory, and trains them jointly for open-domain QA and other fact-heavy tasks?
What did the Lost in the Middle study find about how language model accuracy changes depending on where the relevant information sits in a long context?
Which paper found that language models answer best when the key document is at the start or end of a lengthy prompt and much worse when it is buried in between?
Which retrieval architectures did BEIR find generalize best zero-shot across its 18 datasets, and how did BM25 compare with dense retrievers?
Which paper gathers 18 varied public search datasets to test how well neural search models transfer to new domains without in-domain training, finding BM25 a surprisingly strong baseline?
How does ColBERT's late interaction encode queries and documents separately with BERT while still modeling fine-grained token-level similarity?
Which paper encodes queries and documents separately into per-token vectors and scores pairs by summing each query token's best match, so document vectors can be computed ahead of time?
How does Self-RAG use special reflection tokens to decide when to retrieve and to critique both the retrieved passages and its own outputs?
Which paper trains one language model to decide on demand whether to fetch passages and to emit special tokens that judge the relevance and support of evidence and of its own answers?
How does HyDE use an instruction-following LLM to write a hypothetical document for a query and then embed it with Contriever for zero-shot dense retrieval?
Which paper, needing no supervision at all, has an LLM imagine a plausible answer passage for a query and then uses that invented passage's embedding to look up similar real documents?
What metrics does Ragas use to assess RAG pipelines, such as faithfulness and context relevance, without relying on ground-truth human annotations?
Which framework scores pipelines that combine a search component with an LLM answer writer along faithfulness, context relevance and answer relevance, without needing human-labeled ground truth?
How does GraphRAG build an entity knowledge graph and pre-generated community summaries to answer global questions over a whole corpus?

Which paper answers broad sensemaking questions about an entire document collection by having an LLM build a network of extracted entities, write overviews of related clusters, and combine partial answers?
How does the GPT-2 conversational query rewriter generate weak supervision from ad hoc search sessions using rules and self-supervised learning, and how did it do on TREC CAsT?
Which paper fine-tunes GPT-2 to expand terse follow-up questions from a multi-turn search chat into self-contained ones, producing weak training labels from ordinary web search session logs?
